JCSG-E_Ecoli_GNF_1.name: GNF Ecoli Expression Protocol 1
JCSG-E_Ecoli_GNF_1.text:
Preparative-Scale Expression of JCSG Proteins in E. coli
			1.	INTRODUCTION
			Protocols provided for PepcDB represent the typical practices followed by the JCSG in preparation of proteins for crystallization. Individual details may vary somewhat for any particular target.
			Cloned JCSG targets that have passed small-scale protein expression screening are typically expressed on a preparative scale in E. coli and labeled with selenomethionine to facilitate structure solution. A custom 96-culture fermentor is utilized (2.1), allowing for parallel expression of multiple unique proteins. In the current JCSG expression method, which is described here, 12 different proteins are expressed concurrently and selenomethionine incorporation occurs via methionine biosynthesis pathway inhibition (2.2), which does not require a methionine auxotrophic strain. Cells are grown in a minimal medium that is supplemented, just before induction of expression, with selenomethionine and amino acids known to inhibit methionine biosynthesis.
			The methionine biosynthesis pathway inhibition protocol was initiated in February 2005. Prior to that time, targets were frequently expressed in a defined medium containing all 20 amino acids, with selenomethionine replacing methionine, using the methionine auxotrophic strain DL41 (2.3). In that method, cells were induced at a higher OD600 nm (3-4 at start of induction) as compared to the protocol described here. Furthermore, before July 2005, proteins that could be solved by molecular replacement were expressed in native fermentation medium (described herein for growing overnight cultures). In that process, 1) overnight cultures were smaller (8 ml), 2) an air/oxygen mixture was used (100% air for the first 80 min, followed by 50/50 air/oxygen until start of induction, 2-2.5 hr after start of fermentation, and then 100% oxygen during 3-hr induction), 3) the same medium was used for overnight cultures and fermentation, and 4) cells were induced (4-6 at start of induction) and harvested (18-22 at conclusion of 3-hr induction) at a higher OD600 nm, as compared to the method described here. Finally, prior to July 2005, IPTG was used, albeit infrequently, at a final concentration of 1 mM to induce expression of certain targets.
			2.	REFERENCES
				Multi-sample fermentor and method of using same. U.S. patent nos. 6,723,555 and 6,635,441.
				Van Duyne GD, Standaert RF, Karplus PA, Schreiber SL, Clardy J. Atomic structures of the human immunophilin FKBP-12 complexes with FK506 and rapamycin. J Mol Biol. 1993 Jan 5;229(1):105-24.
				Hendrickson WA, Horton JR, LeMaster DM. Selenomethionyl proteins produced for analysis by multiwavelength anomalous diffraction (MAD): a vehicle for direct determination of three-dimensional structure. EMBO J. 1990 May;9(5):1665-72.
			3.	MATERIALS
				Preparing Stock Solutions
			Use autoclaved, dedicated glassware.
				AG104 analytical balance (Mettler Toledo)
				PB1502-S balance (Mettler Toledo)
				Fisherbrand aluminum foil, heavy-gauge roll, W x L: 18 in. x 50 ft. (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # 01-213-104)

			Q.S. to 50 L with DI H2O.
			Store at room temperature in a Nalgene 50-L polypropylene round carboy with spigot (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # Z360279).

			Q.S. to 50 ml with Milli-Q H2O.
			Sterile filter. Cover with foil (light sensitive). Store at 4C.

			Q.S. to 50 ml with Milli-Q H2O.
			Sterile filter. Cover with foil (light sensitive). Store at 4C.
				0.1 M CaCl2:
			2.94 g CaCl2 dihydrate (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # C5080);
			Q.S. to 200 ml with Milli-Q H2O.
			Sterile filter. Store at room temperature.
				Amino acid solution:
			8.45 g L-phenylalanine (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # P2126);
			8.45 g L-threonine (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # T8625);
			8.45 g L-lysine monohydrochloride (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # L5626);
			4.22 g L-isoleucine (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # I2752); 
			4.22 g L-leucine (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # L8000); 
			4.22 g L-valine (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # V0500); 
			0.42 g L-methionine (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # M9625); 
			Q.S. to 2.2 L with Milli-Q H2O. 
			Sterile filter. Store at 4C.
				20% (w/v) arabinose:
			200 g L-(+)-arabinose (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # A3256);
			Q.S. to 1 L with Milli-Q H2O.
			Sterile filter. Store at 4C.
				100 mg/ml ampicillin: 
			25 g ampicillin sodium salt (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # A9518);
			Q.S. to 250 ml with Milli-Q H2O. 
			Sterile filter. Prepare 10-ml aliquots. Store at -20C.
				30 mg/ml kanamycin: 
			7.5 g kanamycin sulfate (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # K4000);
			Q.S. to 250 ml with Milli-Q H2O. 
			Sterile filter. Prepare 10-ml aliquots. Store at -20C.
				LB broth:
			20 g LB broth (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # L3022);
			Q.S. to 1 L with Milli-Q H2O.
			Autoclave for 45 min in a 1-L Pyrex bottle. Once cool, add 1 ml of 30 mg/ml kanamycin or 100 mg/ml ampicillin. Store at 4C.
				Antifoam 204: 
			500 ml Antifoam 204 (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # A6426).
			Autoclave for 45 min in a 500-ml Pyrex bottle. Store at room temperature.
				TB1 medium:
			168 g Bacto yeast extract (BD, Cat. # 212720, 2 kg);
			84 g tryptone (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # BP1421-2, 2 kg);
			Q.S. to 6 L with Milli-Q H2O.
			Autoclave for 45 min in a 10-L Pyrex bottle. Store at 4C.
				Autoclaved Milli-Q H2O: 
			Autoclave 2 x ~9 L of Milli-Q H2O in 10-L Pyrex bottles. Store at room temperature in a Nalgene 20-L fluorinated carboy with spigot (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # Z260789).
				Lysozyme buffer:
			1 L Trizma hydrochloride solution, 1.00-0.05M, pH 8.0+/-0.05 (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # T3038-1L);
			200 ml 5 M NaCl;
			Q.S. to 20 L with Milli-Q H2O.
			Store at room temperature in a Nalgene 20-L fluorinated carboy with spigot.
				Trace metal solution (5000x): 
			169 mg MnSO4 monohydrate (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # 221287); 
			287.5 mg ZnSO4 heptahydrate (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # Z4750);
			47.6 mg CoCl2 hexahydrate (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # 255599); 
			26.9 mg CuCl2 (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # 222011); 
			47.5 mg NiCl2 hexahydrate (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # N6136); 
			48.4 mg Na2MoO4 dihydrate (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # M1003); 
			52.6 mg Na2SeO3 pentahydrate (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # 00163);
			Q.S. to 100 ml with Milli-Q H2O.
			Autoclave for 45 min in a 100-ml Pyrex bottle. It may be necessary to add concentrated HCl (~one drop) to completely dissolve the metals. Store at room temperature.
				0.5 M MOPS, pH 7.6+/10.1 (prepare 2 x 5 L):
			523 g MOPS (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # BP308-500, 500 g);
			71.13 g NaOH;
			Q.S. to 5 L with Milli-Q H2O.
			Check that pH is 7.6+/-0.1. Sterile filter. Store at 4C.
				Starter Cultures
				Glycerol stocks of interest
				LB broth
				BD Falcon 14-ml polystyrene round-bottom test tubes with snap caps (BD, Cat. # 352057)
				Innova 4430 incubator shaker (New Brunswick Scientific)
				Overnight Cultures
				Fisherbrand aluminum foil, heavy-gauge roll, W x L: 18 in. x 50 ft.
				Fermentor tubes: Nalgene 100-ml high-speed polycarbonate tubes with lip (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # 05-528J)
				GNFermentor tube rack (GNF Systems, http://www.gnfsystems.com/)
				Native fermentation medium: 
			6 L TB1 medium;
			87.5 ml 80% (w/w) glycerol;
			700 ml 0.5 M MOPS, pH 7.6+/-0.1;
			70 ml 5 M NaCl;
			7 ml 30 mg/ml kanamycin or 100 mg/ml ampicillin;
			7 ml Antifoam 204;
			Q.S. to 7 L with autoclaved Milli-Q H2O.
			Store at 4C (this medium can be prepared several days in advance of use).
				Innova 4430 incubator shaker (platform is equipped to accommodate GNFermentor tube rack)
				Preparing Water Bath
				GNFermentor water bath (GNF Systems)
				Fisher Isotemp immersion circulator, model 2100 (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # 13-873-44A)
				Fisherbrand Red-Spirit no-roll thermometer, -20C to 110C (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # 14-997)
				Starting Fermentation
				15 mM FeSO4 (a component of Met inhibition fermentation medium):
			166.81 mg FeSO4 heptahydrate (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. # 215422); 
			Q.S. to 40 ml with Milli-Q H2O.
			Sterile filter.
				Met inhibition fermentation medium:
			4773.3 ml autoclaved Milli-Q H2O; 
			1400 ml 5x M9 medium; 
			700 ml MOPS, pH 7.6+/-0.1;
			14 ml 500x MgSO4;
			87.5 ml 80% (w/w) glycerol;
			7 ml 15 mM FeSO4 (always freshly prepared);
			7 ml Antifoam 204;
			7 ml 30 mg/ml kanamycin or 100 mg/ml ampicillin;
			1.40 ml 0.1 M CaCl2;
			1.40 ml 5000x trace metal solution;
			700 ml vitamin B12 solution;
			700 ul thiamine solution. 
			Store overnight at 4C (this medium is prepared the day before use).
				Nalgene Unwire test tube racks, for 30 mm tubes, 24 places (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # 14-809-49)
				Automated Protein Purification System (GNF Systems)
				Fisherbrand aluminum foil, heavy-gauge roll, W x L: 18 in. x 50 ft.
				Masterflex L/S Digi-Staltic dispensing pump system (Cole-Parmer, Cat. # EW-77310-00)
				Masterflex L/S double-Y tubing system (Cole-Parmer, Cat. # C-96501-35)
				GNFermentor manifold, tube rack, gas flow controller and control valve, and water bath (GNF Systems)
				Oxygen source
				AG104 analytical balance (Mettler Toledo) for preparing 15 mM FeSO4
				Starting Induction
				25 mg/ml selenomethionine (a component of SIMBIC):
			875 mg L-(+)-selenomethionine, analytical grade (Anatrace, Cat. # S2000);
			Q.S. to 35 ml with Milli-Q H2O.
			Sterile filter.
				SIMBIC (Selenomethionine Incorporation by Methionine Biosynthesis Inhibition Cocktail)
			171.5 ml amino acid solution;
			32.5 ml 25 mg/ml selenomethionine (always freshly prepared).
			Keep in refrigerator until use.
				2% (w/v) arabinose:
			40 ml 20% (w/v) arabinose;
			360 ml autoclaved Milli-Q H2O.
				Fisherbrand narrow-stem disposable transfer pipets (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # 13-711-6M)
				LB broth
				Costar 96-well flat well bottom cell culture plate (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # 07-200-91)
				SpectraMax Plus absorbance microplate reader (Molecular Devices)
				AG104 analytical balance (Mettler Toledo) for preparing 25 mg/ml selenomethionine
				During Induction Period
				Approximately 500 ml of autoclaved Milli-Q H2O
				Checking Final ODs
				Fisherbrand narrow-stem disposable transfer pipets
				Costar 96-well flat well bottom cell culture plate
				LB broth
				SpectraMax Plus absorbance microplate reader
				Ending Fermentation
				Fisherbrand absorbent underpads, L x W: 20 x 36 in. (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # 14-206-63)
				Nalgene Unwire test tube racks, for 30 mm tubes, 24 places
				Harvesting Cells
				5 mg/ml lysozyme:
			1.5 g lysozyme, egg white (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # BP535-100, 100 g);
			Q.S. to 300 ml with lysozyme buffer.
			Keep on ice until use (lysozyme solution is prepared just before checking final ODs).
				PB1502-S balance (Mettler Toledo)
				Beckman J6-MC centrifuge (Beckman Coulter)
				Corning 500-ml polypropylene tubes (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # 07-200-621)				Support cushions for 500-ml tubes (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # 07-200-622)
				Beckman Coulter bottle sleeves (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # NC9708671)
				Cleaning GNFermentor and Fermentor Tubes
				Bleach soaking solution:
			40 ml bleach;
			14 L DI H2O.
			Prepare in a Nalgene 14.2-L polypropylene sterilizing tray (Fisher Scientific, Cat. # 13-359-20B).
				Approximately 14 L of 0.1 M NaOH/1% SDS in a Nalgene 14.2-L polypropylene sterilizing tray
				Fisherbrand aluminum foil, heavy-gauge roll, W x L: 18 in. x 50 ft.
				GNFermentor autoclaving box for manifold
			4.	METHODS
				Preparing Stock Solutions
				Prepare stock solutions in advance of the fermentation run.
				Prepare native fermentation medium up to several days in advance of use (to be used for overnight cultures).
				Starter Cultures
			The cultures of the GNFermentor are arranged like a 96-well plate, with eight rows (A-H) and 12 columns (1-12). Twelve different targets are expressed per fermentation run, each in eight cultures. A starter culture is prepared for each of the 12 targets.
				Add 2 ml of LB broth to each of twelve 14-ml round-bottom test tubes.
				Inoculate the medium in each tube with the appropriate glycerol stock.
				Incubate the starter cultures at 250 rpm/37C in the incubator shaker for at least 3 hr.
				Overnight CultureThe 12 starter cultures, each corresponding to a different target, are used to initiate 96 overnight cultures. Media in fermentor tubes A1-H1 are inoculated with the first starter culture (200 ul per tube), A2-H2 with the second, A3-H3 with the third, etc.
				Fill each of the 96 autoclaved fermentor tubes, which are sitting in the GNFermentor tube rack, with 16 ml of native fermentation medium.
				Inoculate the medium in each tube with 200 ul of the appropriate starter culture.
				Cover the tubes with aluminum foil.
				Attach the tube rack containing the 96 fermentor tubes to the platform of the incubator shaker (platform is equipped to accommodate the tube rack).
				Incubate the cultures overnight at 250 rpm/37C.
				Prepare 15 mM FeSO4 (a component of Met inhibition fermentation medium).
				Prepare Met inhibition fermentation medium (to be used the next day for fermentation).
				Preparing Water Bath
				Fill the water bath with DI H2O to a predetermined level such that the cultures will be mostly submerged and the fermentor tubes will not float when the manifold is not placed on top.
				Mount the immersion circulator and thermometer on the side of the water bath.
				Turn on the immersion circulator.
				Set the water bath temperature to 39C. Ensure that this temperature is maintained throughout the fermentation run.
				Starting Fermentation
			The manifold delivers oxygen to 96 fermentor tubes via 96 cannulae. The manifold sits on the fermentor tubes in the tube rack, with a cannula inside each fermentor tube/culture. The oxygen flow into the cultures via the cannulae is sufficient to resuspend the cell pellets of the overnight cultures in Met inhibition fermentation medium.
				Remove the tube rack containing the 96 overnight cultures from the incubator shaker.
				Transfer the overnight cultures to the Nalgene Unwire tube racks.
				Using the Automated Protein Purification System, which can accommodate 96 fermentor tubes, centrifuge the overnight cultures at 3000 rpm (~3000 x g) for 4 min (4 min from the time the rotor reaches 3000 rpm).
				Decant the supernatants.
				Put the 96 fermentor tubes containing the cell pellets back into the GNFermentor tube rack and cover with aluminum foil.
				Program the Masterflex pump to deliver 96 x 65 ml.
				Insert the autoclaved Masterflex tubing into the pump heads.
				Place both ends of the tubing into the Met inhibition fermentation medium and prime the tubing.
				Remove the foil and dispense 65 ml of Met inhibition fermentation medium into each of the 96 fermentor tubes containing the cell pellets.
				Move the tube rack containing the fermentor tubes into the 39C water bath. Wait about 5 min for the media to warm up to ensure that the Antifoam 204 is uniformly dispersed (otherwise, the cultures may bubble over when the oxygen is turned on). The media will appear cloudy when the Antifoam 204 is evenly distributed.
				Place the manifold on the fermentor tubes.
				Attach the tubing that is attached to the gas flow control valve to the manifold.
				Turn the oxygen valve to the on position.
				Program the gas flow controller to deliver 100% oxygen for >300 min and start the fermentation run. The total run time is ~300 min; however, it is best to set a longer time and manually stop the run, in case one of the steps takes longer than expected.
				If the flow rate of oxygen is not 3.6 ft3/min, adjust the gas flow control valve accordingly. Ensure that this flow rate is maintained throughout the fermentation run.
				Starting Induction
				Prepare 25 mg/ml selenomethionine (a component of SIMBIC).
				Prepare SIMBIC.
				Prepare 2% arabinose.
				After 90 min from the time the oxygen flow was turned on, a sample is removed from fermentor tubes A01, B02, C03, D04, E05, and F06, representing random cultures, and their ODs at 600 nm are checked (ODs at 600 nm should be 1.5-2.0). Using a transfer pipet, transfer ~50 l of culture from each of the six fermentor tubes to a flat well bottom plate.
				In the same plate, perform a 1/10 dilution of each sample (30 ul of culture + 270 ul of LB broth). Include a blank (300 ul of LB broth).
				Using the absorbance microplate reader, read the OD at 600 nm.
				Check that the oxygen flow rate is 3.6 ft3/min and that the water bath temperature is 39C. Adjust if necessary.
				After 105 min from the time the oxygen flow was turned on, add 2 ml of SIMBIC to each culture.
				Wait 15 min (120 min after the time the oxygen flow was turned on) and add 4 ml of 2% arabinose to each culture.
				Induce protein expression for 3 hr.
				During Induction Period
				Ensure that the oxygen flow rate is 3.6 ft3/min and that the water bath temperature is 39C. Adjust if necessary.
				Monitor the volume in the tubes, using the 65-ml line drawn around the circumference of the tube as reference. If the culture volumes are low, Q.S. to 65 ml with autoclaved Milli-Q H2O.
				Checking Final ODs
				Prepare 5 mg/ml lysozyme (to be used in 4.10.2).
				After 160 min of induction, a sample is removed from fermentor tubes A01-A12 and E01-E12, representing duplicates of each target, and their ODs at 600 nm are checked (ODs at 600 nm are typically 8-10). Using a transfer pipet, transfer ~50 ul of culture from each of the 24 fermentor tubes to a flat well bottom plate.
				In the same plate, perform a 1/40 dilution of each sample. Prepare a 1/20 dilution of each sample, followed by a 1/2 dilution of each 1/20 dilution (15 ul of culture + 285 ul of LB broth, followed by 150 ul of 1/20 dilution + 150 ul of LB broth). Include a blank (300 ul of LB broth).
				Using the absorbance microplate reader, read the OD at 600 nm.
				Ending Fermentation
			After 3 hr of induction, the run is stopped.
				Turn off the immersion circulator.
				Stop the run using the gas flow controller.
				Turn the oxygen valve to the off position.
				Detach the tubing that is connected to the gas flow control valve from the manifold.
				Carefully lift the manifold off the fermentor tubes and place it in the sink.
				Remove the tube rack containing the 96 cultures from the water bath and place it on an absorbent underpad.
				Transfer the cultures to the Nalgene Unwire tube racks.
				Harvesting Cells
				Place 12 x 500-ml tubes on ice.
				Add 24 ml of 5 mg/ml lysozyme to each of the twelve 500-ml tubes.
				Pool cultures A1-H1 in the first 500-ml tube, A2-H2 in the second, A3-H3 in the third, etc.
				Balance the tubes in pairs by adding Milli-Q H2O. The incubation time with lysozyme is just the time it takes to balance the tubes and load them into the centrifuge.
				Centrifuge the cultures at 4000 rpm for 20 min in a Beckman J6-MC centrifuge equipped with bottle sleeves and support cushions.
				Decant the supernatants into a waste container.
				Store the cell pellets in the 500-ml tubes at -20C.
				Cleaning GNFermentor and Fermentor Tubes
			The Masterflex tubing, manifold, tube rack, and water bath are cleaned as described in 4.11.1-4.11.3. Clean the inside of the manifold/cannulae, also, by forcing water and NaOH/SDS through the gas inlet. The fermentor tubes are cleaned as described in 4.11.6-4.11.11.
				Rinse with DI H2O.
				Wash with 0.1 M NaOH/1% SDS. Using a brush, scrub the surfaces of the manifold, tube rack, and water bath. Soak for a minimum of 20 min.
				Rinse thoroughly with DI H2O.
				Wrap the Masterflex tubing in aluminum foil and put the manifold in its autoclaving box.
				Autoclave the Masterflex tubing and manifold for 45 min. When autoclaving, leave the lid of the autoclaving box slightly open.
				Soak the 96 fermentor tubes overnight in DI H2O.
				Rinse the tubes three times with DI H2O.
				Soak the tubes for a minimum of 1 hr in bleach soaking solution.
				Rinse the tubes once with DI H2O.
				Soak the tubes for a minimum of 1 hr in 0.1 M NaOH/1% SDS.
				Rinse the tubes three times with DI H2O.
				Dry tubes in an inverted position on a clean surface. 
				Put tubes into the GNFermentor tube rack.
				Cover the tubes with aluminum foil.
				Autoclave the tubes for 45 min (do not exceed 121C).
				Keep autoclaved tubes in GNFermentor tube rack until needed for another fermentation run.
				Fermentor tubes are used multiple times. If using new tubes, add 65 ml of DI H2O to each tube. Using a water resistant marker, denote this volume, drawing around the circumference of the tube. Label each tube near its rim. Tubes are labeled A01-A12 through H01-H12. Subsequently, follow steps 4.11.11-4.11.16.

JCSG-TPur_GNF_1.name: GNF Purification Protocol 1
JCSG-TPur_GNF_1.text:
Purification of JCSG Proteins Expressed in E. coli
			Daniel McMullan, Dennis Carlton, Julie Feuerhelm, and Polat Abdubek
			1. INTRODUCTION
			Protocols provided for PepcDB represent the typical practices followed by the JCSG in preparation of proteins for crystallization. Individual details may vary somewhat for any particular target.
			This protocol describes the parallel purification of 24 unique proteins. Protein expression was performed using a custom 96-culture fermentor (described in 'Preparative-Scale Expression of JCSG Proteins in E. coli' protocol). For the expression of 24 unique proteins, two fermentations were performed, where each target protein was expressed in eight cultures. The eight cultures corresponding to a particular target protein were pooled into a single 500-ml conical centrifuge bottle, and the cells were harvested. The resulting 24 cell pellets, each corresponding to a unique protein, were stored in a -20 C freezer. Each protein was expressed with an N-terminal expression and purification tag (MGSDKIHHHHHH) followed by a tobacco etch virus (TEV) protease cleavage site (ENLYFQG).
			Variations to this protocol have been used in the past (2.1, 2.2), primarily before 2005. Examples include (a) use of an uncleavable expression and purification tag (MGSDKIHHHHHH), (b) employment of RESOURCE Q and Superdex 200 columns, (c) utilization of Talon and POROS HQ resins, (d) use of Tris- and PO4-based buffers, and (e) performance of sonication using the Automated Protein Purification System (GNF Systems), a custom robot equipped with ultrasonic processors (Sonics and Materials, Inc.).
			2. REFERENCES
			2.1. McMullan D, Canaves JM, Quijano K, Abdubek P, Nigoghossian E, Haugen J, Klock HE, Vincent J, Hale J, Paulsen J, Lesley SA. High-throughput protein production for X-ray crystallography and use of size exclusion chromatography to validate or refute computational biological unit predictions. J Struct Funct Genomics. 2005;6(2-3):135-41.
			2.2. DiDonato M, Deacon AM, Klock HE, McMullan D, Lesley SA. A scaleable and integrated crystallization pipeline applied to mining the Thermotoga maritima proteome. J Struct Funct Genomics. 2004;5(1-2):133-46.
			2.3. Klock HE, Koesema EJ, Knuth MW, Lesley SA. Combining the polymerase incomplete primer extension method for cloning and mutagenesis with microscreening to accelerate structural genomics efforts. Proteins. 1 May 2008;71(2):982-994.
			3. MATERIALS
			Measure pH of buffers at room temperature. Adjust pH of buffers with NaOH (pH of HEPES stock solution is 7.3). Store buffers in cold room. Add TCEP to buffers immediately before use.
			3.1. Buffers and Solutions
			3.1.1. HEPES Lysis Buffer: 50 mM HEPES pH 8.0+-0.1, 50 mM NaCl, 10 mM imidazole, 1 mM Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine hydrochloride (TCEP; BioVectra, catalog # 1300)
			3.1.2. HEPES Wash Buffer: 50 mM HEPES pH 8.0, 300 mM NaCl, 40 mM imidazole, 10% (v/v) glycerol, 1 mM TCEP
			3.1.3. HEPES Elution Buffer: 20 mM HEPES pH 8.0, 300 mM imidazole, 10% (v/v) glycerol, 1 mM TCEP	3.1.4. HEPES Crystallization Buffer: 20 mM HEPES pH 8.0, 200 mM NaCl, 40 mM imidazole, 1 mM TCEP
			3.1.5. 100 mM NiCl2
			3.1.6. 100 mM EDTA; used only to regenerate nickel-chelating resin columns
			3.1.7. 1 N NaOH; used only to regenerate nickel-chelating resin columns
			3.2. Equipment
			3.2.1. Homogenizer (Omni International, catalog # TH115)
			3.2.2. Saw Tooth (Fine) Generator Probe, 10 mm x 195 mm, 316 stainless steel (Omni International, catalog # G10-195)
			3.2.3. Microfluidizer Processor (Microfluidics, catalog # M110L)
			3.2.4. Masterflex Digi-staltic pump
			3.2.5. Criterion Dodeca Cell (Bio-Rad, catalog # 165-4130)
			3.2.6. Sorvall Evolution RC Superspeed Centrifuge with SA-600 rotor
			3.2.7. Sorvall RC 12BP Centrifuge with H-12000 rotor
			3.3. Additional Materials
			3.3.1. AcTEV Protease, 10,000 units (Invitrogen, catalog # 12575-023)
			3.3.2. Criterion Tris-HCl Gel, 4-20%, 12+2 Well Comb, 45 ul Samples (Bio-Rad, catalog # 345-0032)
			3.3.3. Amicon Ultra-15 Centrifugal Filter Units, Ultracel regenerated cellulose membrane, 5-kDa cutoff, 24/pk (Millipore, catalog # UFC900524)
			3.3.4. HiLoad 16/60 Superdex 200 or HiLoad 16/60 Superdex 75 column (GE Healthcare, catalog # 17-1069-01 or 17-1068-01, respectively); used only as necessary
			3.3.5. Econo-Pac Chromatography Columns, empty, 500/pk, frits are included (Bio-Rad, catalog # 732-1011); used only to prepare new nickel-chelating resin columns
			3.3.6. Chelating Sepharose Fast Flow, 5 L (GE Healthcare, catalog # 17-0575-04); used only to prepare new nickel-chelating resin columns
			3.3.7. Disposable PD-10 Desalting Columns, 30/pk (GE Healthcare, catalog # 17-0851-01)
			3.3.8. Coomassie Plus Assay Kit (Pierce, catalog # 23236)
			3.3.9. Oak Ridge Centrifuge Tubes, PC, 50 ml, 10/pk (Nalgene, catalog # 3118-0050)
			3.3.10. Shodex KW803 analytical SEC column
			4. METHODS
			Perform all steps at 4 C unless otherwise indicated. Bradford assays and SDS-PAGE are performed at room temperature. Use cold buffers.
			4.1. Lysis and Clarification
			Using a custom robot, cell lysis is achieved by homogenization coupled with the use of a Microfluidizer. The robot is equipped with a homogenizer/probe and a Microfluidizer, which are commercially available (see 3.2.1-3.2.3), and can serially process 12 cell pellets, each contained in a 500-ml conical centrifuge bottle, in 2 hr. The 24 cell pellets (see 1) are processed in two groups of 12. Alternatively, this process can be performed without the robot using the commercially available homogenizer/probe and Microfluidizer. Follow the manufacturers' instructions for utilization of these instruments.
			4.1.1. Remove 12 bottles containing 12 cell pellets from the -20 C freezer.
			4.1.2. Thaw the cell pellets. Bottles can be placed in a room-temperature water bath to accelerate thawing. 
			4.1.3. Add 80 ml of HEPES Lysis Buffer to each bottle using a Masterflex pump.
			4.1.4. Place the 12 bottles in the 4 C water bath.
			4.1.5. Each of the cell pellets is lysed as follows. 
			4.1.5.1. Homogenize the pellet and Lysis Buffer for 81 sec (nine cycles x nine sec per cycle) at 35,000 rpm (maximum setting) using the homogenizer/probe. Each cycle consists of 6 sec with the probe near the bottom of the homogenate followed by 3 sec with the probe near the surface.
			4.1.5.2. Pass the homogenate through the Microfluidizer, collecting into the original bottle. The air pressure requirement and process pressure are 80 and 18,000 psi, respectively. 
			4.1.5.2.1. If the robot is not used: To maximize recovery of the lysate, it is recommended to pass Lysis Buffer through the Microfluidizer. Collect this pass-through into the bottle containing the lysate. The resulting volume will not fit into three Oak Ridge tubes (see 4.1.6.1).
			4.1.5.2.2. When using the robot: Do not perform 4.1.5.2.1, since the Microfluidizer associated with the robot has been modified such that it will expel virtually all of the lysate.
			4.1.5.3. Clean the homogenizer probe by briefly submerging it in HEPES Lysis Buffer and running the motor. 
			4.1.5.4. Clean the Microfluidizer by passing HEPES Lysis Buffer through it, collecting the pass-through into a waste vessel. Repeat. 
			4.1.6. The 12 lysates are clarified in groups of four, when four become available, as follows. 
			4.1.6.1. Transfer each of the four lysates into three Oak Ridge centrifuge tubes (~30 ml of lysate per tube).
			4.1.6.2. Centrifuge the four lysates (contained in 12 Oak Ridge centrifuge tubes) for 30 min in an SA-600 rotor at 15,000 rpm (32,572 x g) using a Sorvall Evolution RC Superspeed Centrifuge. The clarified lysates are loaded onto nickel-chelating resin columns as they become available (see 4.2.1).
			4.1.7. Repeat 4.1.1-4.1.6 for the second set of 12 cell pellets.
			4.2. Purification with Nickel-chelating Resin and Buffer Exchange
			Clarified cell lysates are purified at 4 C using metal-affinity liquid chromatography. Target proteins containing the purification tag (see 1) are bound, washed, and eluted into a small desalting column for buffer exchange prior to TEV digestion.
			4.2.1. The 24 clarified lysates (three supernatants per lysate) are loaded onto nickel-chelating resin columns in groups of four, when four become available, as follows. Two nickel-chelating resin columns are used per lysate (target protein).
			4.2.1.1. Decant each of the four clarified lysates onto two gravity-fed 1.5-ml nickel-chelating resin columns pre-equilibrated with HEPES Lysis Buffer (~45 ml of clarified lysate per column). Collect each flow-through into a waste tray.
			4.2.2. The 48 nickel-chelating resin columns are washed as described in 4.2.2.1-4.2.2.2 and the flow-throughs are collected into a waste tray. Subsequently, the target proteins are eluted as described in 4.2.2.3.
			4.2.2.1. Add 7.5 ml of HEPES Wash Buffer onto each column.
			4.2.2.2. Add 0.5 ml of HEPES Elution Buffer.
			4.2.2.3. Add 2.5 ml of HEPES Elution Buffer. Collect the eluate directly onto a PD-10 column pre-equilibrated with HEPES Crystallization Buffer. Two PD-10 columns are used per target protein.
			4.2.3. Proteins are eluted from the 48 PD-10 columns as described in 4.2.3.1-4.2.3.2.
			4.2.3.1. For each target protein, add 3.5 ml of HEPES Crystallization Buffer onto the first PD-10 column, collecting the eluate into a 50-ml conical tube.
			4.2.3.2. Add 3.5 ml of HEPES Crystallization Buffer onto the second PD-10 column, collecting this eluate into the tube containing the first eluate. Consequently, for every target protein, the two PD-10 eluates are combined (pool = 7 ml).
			4.2.4. Remove 200 ul of each of the 24 PD-10 eluates for Bradford assay. This aliquot will be used for SDS-PAGE analysis, also, if the target protein will be dropped because the yield is too low (see 4.3).
			4.2.5. Determine the protein concentrations of the 24 PD-10 eluates using Coomassie Plus Assay Reagent.
			4.3. TEV Digestion
			For target proteins predetermined to be uncleavable by TEV protease based on microscreening, proceed to Step 4.5 (i.e. skip 4.3 and 4.4). For a given target protein, if the protein concentration is ~0.5 mg/ml (~3.5 mg), do not process it further. Up to 30 mg of PD-10 eluate protein are digested. If the yield is ~30 mg, digest all of the protein. For every 15 mg of protein to be digested, 1 mg of TEV protease is added. Recombinant TEV is produced internally and adjusted to 1 mg/ml. Invitrogen's acTEV can also be used. The concentration of acTEV is in the range of 0.303-0.714 mg/ml based on a specific activity of 14-33 U/ug and a unit concentration of 10 U/ul, as per Invitrogen. For example, when digesting less than =30 mg of protein, the entire PD-10 eluate (7 ml) will be combined with either 2 ml of in-house TEV or 4 ml of 0.5 mg/ml acTEV (no buffer is added in either case). When using 0.5 mg/ml acTEV, the final volume will be 11 ml. Consequently, the nickel reverse FT/W will be 12.5 ml instead of 10.5 ml (see 4.4).
			4.3.1. Each of the 24 target proteins are digested as follows.
			4.3.1.1. Calculate the volumes of PD-10 eluate, HEPES Crystallization Buffer, and TEV protease to combine such that the final volume will be 9 ml. When less than =30 mg of protein are digested, the whole PD-10 eluate (7 ml) is combined with 2 ml (2 mg) of in-house TEV (no buffer is added). Buffer is only added when the volume of TEV and PD-10 eluate, once combined, is less than 9 ml.
			4.3.1.2. Combine appropriate volumes of PD-10 eluate and HEPES Crystallization Buffer in a 15-ml conical tube. Invert the tube gently to mix.
			4.3.1.3. Remove 100 ul of the PD-10 eluate-HEPES Crystallization Buffer mixture for SDS-PAGE analysis.
			4.3.1.4. Add TEV protease to the PD-10 eluate-HEPES Crystallization Buffer mixture (final volume = 9 ml). Invert the tube gently to mix.
			4.3.1.5. Incubate the PD-10 eluate-HEPES Crystallization Buffer-TEV protease mixture at room temperature for 2 hr. Subsequently, incubate overnight (~15 hr) at 4 C.
			4.4. Reverse Purification with Nickel-chelating Resin
			Usually, the tag is successfully cleaved by TEV protease. Consequently, when the target protein is reapplied to nickel-chelating resin, it does not bind. Conversely, the cleaved tag and TEV protease, which both contain a His tag, bind to the resin. In some cases, the target protein will adsorb to the resin. This generally occurs due to unsuccessful cleavage of the tag.
			4.4.1. Pour each of the 24 PD-10 eluate-HEPES Crystallization Buffer-TEV protease mixtures (9 ml each) onto a gravity-fed 1.5-ml nickel-chelating resin column pre-equilibrated with HEPES Crystallization Buffer. Collect each flow-through (nickel reverse flow-though) into a 50-ml conical tube.
			4.4.2. The 24 nickel-chelating resin columns are washed as described in 4.4.2.1. Subsequently, elution buffer is applied to the columns as described in 4.4.2.2.
			4.4.2.1. Add 1.5 ml of HEPES Crystallization Buffer onto each column. Collect each flow-through (nickel reverse wash) into the tube containing the corresponding nickel reverse flow-through. Consequently, for each target protein, the nickel reverse flow-through and nickel reverse wash are combined (nickel reverse FT/wash).
			4.4.2.2. Add 10.5 ml of HEPES Elution Buffer onto each column, collecting each eluate (nickel reverse eluate) into a 50-ml conical tube.
			4.4.3. Remove 200 ul of each nickel reverse FT/wash and 200 ul of each nickel reverse eluate for SDS-PAGE analysis, Bradford assay, and analytical SEC.
			4.4.4. Analyze the nickel reverse FT/washs, nickel reverse eluates, and PD-10 eluates (see 4.3.1.3 or 4.2.4) by SDS-PAGE using a Criterion Dodeca Cell and Criterion 4-20% Gels.
			4.4.5. Review the SDS-PAGE data to determine whether a given target protein is in the nickel reverse FT/wash or in the nickel reverse eluate.
			4.4.6. Weigh each nickel reverse FT/wash or nickel reverse eluate, depending on where the target protein was found, to accurately measure its volume, assuming 1 g = 1 ml.
			4.4.7. Determine the protein concentration of each nickel reverse FT/wash or nickel reverse eluate, depending on where the target protein was found, using Coomassie Plus Assay Reagent.
			4.5. Concentrating the Protein
			For each of the 24 target proteins, the appropriate fraction (nickel reverse FT/wash or nickel reverse eluate) is concentrated to a predetermined target volume (volume at which protein concentration is 15 mg/ml) in a centrifugal filter device. Nickel reverse eluates are first buffer exchanged in these devices such that the original buffer is diluted ~225-fold (~152).
			4.5.1. For each target protein, in an Excel spreadsheet, enter the starting concentration, the starting volume (generally 10.5 ml), and the target concentration (15 mg/ml). Calculate the target volume.
			4.5.2. For each target protein, transfer the appropriate fraction (nickel reverse FT/wash or nickel reverse eluate) into an Amicon Ultra-15 centrifugal filter unit with a 5 kDa cutoff.
			4.5.3. Concentrate each nickel reverse FT/wash to the predetermined target volume by centrifugation in an H-12000 rotor at 4000 x g (maximum g-force for the concentrator device; 3471 rpm) using a Sorvall RC 12BP Centrifuge.
			4.5.4. Each nickel reverse eluate is buffer exchanged and concentrated as follows.
			4.5.4.1. Concentrate the nickel reverse eluate to 1 ml as described in 4.5.3.
			4.5.4.2. Add 14 ml of HEPES Crystallization Buffer to the concentrated protein.
			4.5.4.3. Repeat 4.5.4.1.
			4.5.4.4. Repeat 4.5.4.2.
			4.5.4.5. Concentrate the buffer exchanged nickel reverse eluate to the predetermined target volume as described in 4.5.3.
			4.5.5. Once the predetermined target volume is reached, transfer each target protein from the centrifugal filter unit into a 1.5-ml tube or, if necessary, two tubes. Using a black Sharpie, write the appropriate Protein ID number (PID) on each 1.5-ml tube.
			4.5.6. Weigh the 24 concentrated target proteins to accurately measure their volumes, assuming 1 g = 1 ml.
			4.5.7. Determine the protein concentrations of the 24 concentrated target proteins using Coomassie Plus Assay Reagent.
			4.6. Preparing Aliquots of the Protein and Freezing
			For each target protein, if the protein concentration is 15+-5 mg/ml (10-20 mg/ml), perform 4.6.1-4.6.3. If, however, the protein concentration is less than 10 mg/ml, concentrate the target protein further. Use a centrifugal filter unit designed for smaller volumes if necessary. A minimum yield of two 65-ul aliquots with a protein concentration of 8 mg/ml (1.0 mg) is required. If this yield requirement is not met, do not process the target protein further.
			4.6.1. Prepare, in 0.5-ml tubes, four 65-ul aliquots of the concentrated protein for crystallization trials and one 10-ul aliquot for quality control (QC aliquot). If the yield does not allow for four 65-ul aliquots, prepare two or three. Any remaining volume will be flash-frozen in the 1.5-ml tube (bulk tube) or tubes. Using a black Sharpie, write the appropriate PID on each 0.5-ml tube.
			4.6.2. Flash-freeze the aliquots, including bulk tubes, in liquid nitrogen.
			4.6.3. Transfer the frozen aliquots to a -80 C freezer.
			4.7. Quality Control
			Prior to their release for crystallization trials, the 24 target proteins are characterized by LC/MS, analytical SEC, and SDS-PAGE. Generally, multiple species are observed in LC/MS, corresponding to different levels of selenomethionine incorporation. Furthermore, after successful TEV protease cleavage of a given target protein, glycine, which is the last residue of the cleavage site, is left on the N-terminus of the protein. If TEV cleavage is unsuccessful, the N-terminal Met of the expression and purification tag is generally absent. If the molecular weight(s) determined by LC/MS do not match the expected one(s), the target protein is placed in a holding pen. For a given target protein, the observed mass must be within +-1 Da for every 10 kDa. For example, for a 30-kDa protein, the observed mass has to be within 3 Da. A Shodex KW803 column and a Dionex HPLC are used for analytical SEC (2.3).
			4.7.1. For each target protein, transfer 90 ul of preconcentrated nickel reverse FT/wash or nickel reverse eluate (do not dilute), depending on where the target protein was found, into an autosampler plate. Analyze 60 ul by analytical SEC.
			4.7.2. For each target protein, dilute the 10-ul QC aliquot to 100 ul (i.e. ten-fold dilution) with HEPES Crystallization Buffer and analyze as follows.
			4.7.2.1. Analyze 20 ul by SDS-PAGE.
			4.7.2.2. Submit 20 ul for LC/MS.
			4.7.2.3. Transfer 60 ul into an autosampler plate and analyze 40 ul by analytical SEC.
			4.8. Preparative SEC
			Based on analytical SEC or SDS-PAGE, the operator may decide to purify a given target protein further by preparative SEC (not performed frequently). For example, preparative SEC would be performed if analytical SEC showed a large percentage of aggregate. Yield will also influence the decision (i.e. would probably not perform SEC if the yield was low). Typically, a Superdex 200 column and a Dionex HPLC are employed for preparative SEC. However, a Superdex 75 column may be used for target proteins having an in-solution molecular weight of less than 70 kDa (estimated from analytical SEC).
			4.8.1. If the target protein was frozen, thaw all aliquots and combine.
			4.8.2. Adjust volume of target protein to 2.5 ml.
			4.8.3. Load the protein onto a 120-ml Superdex 200 or Superdex 75 column pre-equilibrated with HEPES Crystallization Buffer.
			4.8.4. Elute the protein with one column volume of HEPES Crystallization Buffer. The first 30 ml are diverted to waste. Collect the remaining 90 ml as forty-five 2-ml fractions.
			4.8.5. Pool the peak fractions based on the chromatogram.
			4.8.6. Weigh the combined fractions to accurately measure the volume, assuming 1 g = 1 ml.
			4.8.7. Determine the protein concentration of the pooled fractions using Coomassie Plus Assay Reagent.
			4.8.8. Concentrate/aliquot as described for nickel reverse FT/washs in 4.5 and 4.6. Analyze the QC aliquot (after preparative SEC) as described in 4.7.2.
			4.9. Preparing Nickel-chelating Resin Columns
			Seventy-two nickel-chelating resin columns are needed for this protocol. Columns are used three times and regenerated before the second and third uses. After three uses, the columns are discarded. Two 300-ml slurries of resin are prepared for new columns: one in HEPES Lysis Buffer, the other in HEPES Crystallization Buffer. The unused resin slurries are stored and used when more columns are needed.
			4.9.1. Prepare each of two 300-ml slurries of resin as follows.
			4.9.1.1. Transfer 300 ml of Chelating Sepharose Fast Flow slurry (in 20% EtOH) into a 500-ml conical bottle. The slurry is approximately 75% (v/v) from the manufacturer (300 ml of slurry ~ 225 ml of resin).
			4.9.1.2. Centrifuge the slurry for 3 min at 1600 rpm in an H-12000 rotor using a Sorvall RC 12BP Centrifuge.
			4.9.1.3. Carefully pour off the liquid.
			4.9.1.4. Add deionized H2O to a final volume of 500 ml.
			4.9.1.5. Mix briefly by gently inverting the bottle.
			4.9.1.6. Repeat 4.9.1.2-4.9.1.5.
			4.9.1.7. Repeat 4.9.1.2-4.9.1.3.
			4.9.1.8. Using the graduation marks on the bottle, determine the volume of resin (should be ~200 ml).
			4.9.1.9. Add an equal volume of 100 mM NiCl2 to the resin.
			4.9.1.10. Mix the 50% (v/v) slurry for 5 min by gentle inversion of the bottle.
			4.9.1.11. Repeat 4.9.1.2-4.9.1.5 twice.
			4.9.1.12. Repeat 4.9.1.2-4.9.1.3.
			4.9.1.13. Determine the volume of resin using the graduation marks on the bottle (should be ~200 ml).
			4.9.1.14. Add an equal volume of the appropriate buffer to the resin.
			4.9.1.14.1. If the resin is to be used for first purification step, add HEPES Lysis Buffer.
			4.9.1.14.2. If the resin is to be used for reverse purification, add HEPES Crystallization Buffer.
			4.9.1.15. Repeat 4.9.1.5.
			4.9.1.16. Repeat 4.9.1.2-4.9.1.3.
			4.9.1.17. Repeat 4.9.1.14.
			4.9.2. Using the resin slurries prepared in 4.9.1, pack new nickel-chelating resin columns as follows.
			4.9.2.1. Transfer 3 ml of the 50% (v/v) slurry of Chelating Sepharose Fast Flow (1.5 ml of resin) into each empty Econo-Pac column. Ensure an even suspension of the slurry throughout this step (i.e. do not allow the resin to settle). Collect each flow-through into a waste tray. Store any leftover resin slurry in the buffer in the cold room.
			4.9.2.2. Insert a frit on top of each resin bed.
			4.9.3. Regenerate each used nickel-chelating resin column as follows, collecting the flow-through into a waste tray.
			4.9.3.1. Add 8 ml of 100 mM EDTA onto the column.
			4.9.3.2. Add 8 ml of 1 N NaOH.
			4.9.3.3. Add 5 ml of deionized H2O.
			4.9.3.4. Add 5 ml of 100 mM NiCl2.
			4.9.3.5. Add 5 ml of deionized H2O.
			4.9.3.6. Add 7.5 ml of the appropriate buffer.
			4.9.3.6.1. If the column is to be used for first purification step, add HEPES Lysis Buffer.
			4.9.3.6.2. If the column is to be used for reverse purification, add HEPES Crystallization Buffer.

MCSG-anl_PreInfo-Low Density.name: anl_PreInfo-Low Density
MCSG-anl_PreInfo-Low Density.text:
Argone National Laboratory Protein Purification Protocol-PreInfoLowDensity

After low_density expression as described in SOPSetMetExprn, cell pellets are either sonicated or
lyzed with lysozyme, and subject to the subsequent choromotography steps.


The standard purification protocol includes the following chromatographic steps:
 (a) IMAC-I (immobilized metal affinity chromatography) using a 5-ml HiTrap Chelating HP column (Amersham Biosciences) 
     charged with Ni+2 following factory-recommended procedures.
 (b) Buffer-exchange chromatography on a HiPrep 26/10 desalting column (Amersham Biosciences). 
 (c) His6-tag cleavage using the recombinant TEV protease expressed from the vector pRK508 (a gift from Dr D. Waugh, NCI) 
     and purified using a procedure described earlier. The protease is added at an approximate ratio of 1 mg protease
     per 50 mg of target protein and incubated at 4  degree for 16-24 h. 
 (d) IMAC-II using a 1-ml HiTrap Chelating column(Amersham Biosciences) charged with Ni+2 following factory-recommended procedures.
 (e) Buffer-exchange chromatography on a customized desalting column, the Sephadex G-25 Fine 26/20 XK (Amersham Biosciences).
 Steps (a) and (b) were performed on the AKTA EXPLORER 3D system and steps (d) and (e) on AKTA FPLC 3D (see Results and discussion).



Please use the following publications for reference:

1) Kim Y, Dementieva I, Zhou M, Wu R, Lezondra L, Quartey P, Joachimiak G, Korolev O, Li H, Joachimiak A. 
Automation of protein purification for structural genomics.
J Struct Funct Genomics. 2004;5(1-2):111-8

2) Millard CS, Stols L, Quartey P, Kim Y, Dementieva I, Donnelly MI.
A less laborious approach to the high-throughput production of recombinant proteins in Escherichia coli using 2-liter plastic bottles.
Protein Expr Purif. 2003;29(2):311-20.

MCSG-anl_cloning_1.text:
Ligation independent cloning (LIC) technique,  well suited for high-throughput
automation is employed. Target DNA is amplified using PCR. PCR primers are
designed to append sequences that, after treatment with T4 DNA
polymerase in the presence of single deoxyribonucleotide triphosphate,
generate 12- to 15-base-pair overhangs that are complementary to overhangs
generated in the vector.

Main vectors used are pMCSG7 and pMCSG19:

pMCSG7 is a pET expression vector with His6 tag in 23-aa N-terminal fusion
peptide, with TEV protease cleavage site.

MCSG-standard cloning_ANL.name: standard cloning_ANL
MCSG-standard cloning_ANL.text:
Day 1:  Setup PCR plate, and run it in the thermocycler overnight.


This protocol will produce a well volume of 51 L:
	0.26 mM each primer
1x buffer
	0.2 mM each dNTP
	1 mM MgSO4
	0.016 U/L KOD polymerase

Notes:  	- Different gDNAs will be used in different wells, as specified in the plate design.  
- gDNA is added in the amount of  8.333 ng/well.  Stock gDNA should be 100 ng/L. 
- KOD polymerase should not be thawed.  It is a glycerol solution, and you can pipet it at -20C.
- KOD polymerase is HotStart; inactive until heated.  Not necessary to add the polymerase last.

Hazards:  Normal Precautions.


1.	Begin thawing reagents:
10x KOD buffer
dNTPs
MgSO4
gDNA
primer plates

2.	Prepare a master mix according to the PCR Setup spreadsheet.  Keep on ice at all times.

3.	Divide the master mix into different segments for the different gDNAs, as specified in the spreadsheet.

4.	Dispense 40 L of the correct PCR reaction mix into each well in the PCR plate.  

5.	Keep PCR plate on ice, and run program primersetup to add primers.

6.	Centrifuge plate briefly to ensure all liquid is at the bottom of the wells.

7.	Run program KOD1 in thermocycler.

Denature	    95C for 3 minutes
Cycle(32x)   	    95C for 40 seconds
    53C for 40 seconds
    72C for 1.5 minutes (depends on anticipated product length)
Polish	    72C for 5-10 minutes
Store	    4C overnight.

Runtime:  ~2 hours and 30 minutes





Day 2:  Verify PCR with Picogreen assay.  Purify PCR products.  



Hazards:  No data are available addressing the mutagenicity or toxicity of Quant-iT PicoGreen dsDNA reagent. Because this reagent binds to nucleic acids, it should be treated as a potential mutagen and handled with appropriate care. The DMSO stock solution should be handled with particular caution as DMSO is known to facilitate the entry of organic molecules into tissues.  PicoGreen manual.
-	Try to avoid any contamination of PicoGreen, clean up spills immediately, change gloves if any spills occur.  Change gloves after procedure.

Notes:  PicoGreen has a high freezing point, and takes a while to thaw.
	The data from FluoroStar is delivered by rows, while SG data is usually kept in columns.  The data must be re-sorted before pasting into your SG### spreadsheet.

1.	At least 20 minutes prior to setup, take the Picogreen dye out of the fridge and allow it to thaw at room temperature, in a dark location.  

2.	Assemble materials.  
PCR frags plate
TE buffer, 25 mL
Black flat bottom 96 well plate
Reservoir with water
Reservoir for diluted PicoGreen

3.	Dilute PicoGreen reagent.  25mL of TE are mixed with 125 l of picogreen dye for every two plates processed.  Be sure to use this mixture immediately.  It is light sensitive; therefore the longer it sits out in the light, the more your results will be affected.

4.	Run Multimek program PicoG1.  Setup as below:

5.	 

6.	Setup Fluorostar software.
Open program.  Highlight User and click Run.
Set mode to Fluorescence.  (box in bottom left of window)

7.	Open the top of the FluoroStar machine and rotate the cords so the Fluorescence cords (silver cords) are at the top. 

8.	Open the Fluoro tray (button at top of window).  Place the fluorescent plate.  Close the Fluoro tray.

9.	Start the program.
Click on the Traffic Signal icon.
Select the Picogreen Assay program, and press Ok.  
Name your experiment run.
Click Start Test Run.

10.	Your results are put into an Excel spreadsheet.  
	Access this spreadsheet by clicking the Microsoft Excel icon in the toolbar.
	In the spreadsheet, select your test run and double click.












Overview:  Remove primers and dNTPs from the PCR products.  
End result is your gDNA and amplified genes, in 150 L of TE buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA) or EB buffer (10 mM TrisCl, pH 8.5).  Be careful if eluting with TE, the EDTA may inhibit subsequent reactions.

Hazards:  Robot; keep clear.

Notes:  Watch the robot to make sure that all vacuum steps are performed as expected.  It is especially important that the PE buffer is all pulled through before you add EB / TE.

Materials:
	PM, PE, and TE buffers
	QiaQuick (purple) filter
	Deepwell plate
	Skirted PCR plate

1.	Open the Biomek software, and open program PCR Purification.  Setup the table as indicated in program.
a.	Put your PCR plate in the drilled bottom plate.
b.	Be sure to fill the PE reservoir to the brim, the program uses a lot.

2.	Run the program.  Be sure to turn on vacuum and vacuum switch as instructed, and to blot when instructed.  If you have filled the PE reservoir to the brim, there is no need for the mid-procedure refill. 

3.	Be sure to turn the vacuum pump off.
Day 3:  Make your PCR fragments LIC-ready.  Perform LIC and transform into BL-21 cells.

LIC Overview:  Use the 3 to 5 exonuclease activity of T4 polymerase to create overhangs on your PCR frags.  Combine 32 L of PCR pur with 10.8 L of LIC rxn mix.  Final concentrations of LIC reaction in plate:
		0.94x T4 polymerase buffer
		2.21mM dCTP
		4.34mM DTT
		2 units T4 DNA polymerase (0.05U/L)

Notes:  This procedure is modified.  No mineral oil, no PCR pur dilution.

Hazards:  Robot; keep hands clear.  DTT is an irritant and health hazard; avoid contact.

Materials:  	2 skirted 96 well plates
			LIC reaction materials
8.	Make LIC Reaction mix as follows for two plates:
1000L 	10x T4 Polymerase buffer
232.5L 	100mM dCTP
45.6L 	1M DTT
1160L 	Water
200L		2.5U/l T4 DNA Polymerase (Novagen-LIC quality)
2638L	Total

9.	Array 10.8 l of LIC reaction mix into the labeled MJ Thermocycler plates.  

10.	Multimek  Run program LICxGC.  This will transfer 32 L of PCR pur to the LIC plate, and pipet mix.
11.	 

12.	Foil seal the plates.  Incubate at RT for 30 min (up to an hour is permissible).

13.	Inactivate enzyme by incubating at 75C for 20 min.  

14.	Store at 4C short term, -20C for up to several months, or -80C for even longer periods.
Overview:  Anneal the prepared insert into the prepared vector.  Then transform and plate.

Hazards:  LIC insert solution contains DTT.

Materials: 	48-well LB/amp plates
			Competent cells, 5 mL / plate (10 mL for 2 plates)
			Vector
1.	 Begin gently thawing comp cells on ice.  Label new plate for annealing.

2.	Array vector into annealing plate.

3.	Add LIC prepared insert, 4 L per well.

4.	Incubate at RT for 10 minutes (5 minutes to 1 hour is ok).  

5.	Incubate on ice for 2 minutes.  

6.	Add competent cells, 55 L per well.

7.	Incubate on ice for 5 minutes, to allow cells to recover.

8.	Heat shock at 48C for 45 seconds, to make cells receptive.

9.	Incubate on ice for 2 minutes.

10.	Add LB medium (SOC is preferable), 60 L per well (or up to 120 L)

11.	Incubate at 37C for 30 minutes (up to 1 hour is ok).  While they are incubating, prewarm the agar plates.

12.	Plate 60 L.  Leave plates uncovered to dry, then invert and incubate at 37C for ~14 hr.  Plates must be dried to separate individual colonies.

MCSG-standard expression_ANL.name: standard expression_ANL
MCSG-standard expression_ANL.text:
Overview:  Grow cultures, induce protein expression.

Materials: 	M9 components.
			Deepwell plates
			Thermocycler plates

Notes:  The red solution includes 100 mg/mL amp.

Day 1:  Starter Culture.  Start procedure in the afternoon.
1.	Warm growth plates.  Thaw amp.

2.	Add ampicillin 100ug/mL to LB.  Array LB broth 1 mL/well into your deepwell plate.

3.	Using a multichannel pipet tip, select a single colony from each agar plate square, and inoculate the appropriate well the growth plate.  Leave tip in.  Repeat on a new plate, so you have an A and B clone.  

4.	Leave tips in, and cover with breathable sealing tape.  Incubate overnight 37C, shaking.

Day 2:  Induction
1.	Noon:  make M9 media.  
979 mL water
10 mL mineral supplement solution
10 mL 50% glycerol solution
1 mL Kan + Amp + vitamin solution
1 pouch of M9 salts
1 L total

2.	Array 1mL/well into a deepwell plate.  This is your induction plate.

3.	Inoculate the induction plate with 40L of your starter culture.  Centrifuge remaining starter culture at 1700rcf for 15 minutes.  Dump supernatant, freeze pellets for later plasmid purification.

4.	Incubate at 37C, shaking, for 4 hours until the OD600 is 0.8 -1.

5.	Turn temperature down to 4C, incubate for 30 min.

6.	Mix 40L of induction plate with 40L of 50% glycerol.  Freeze this glycerol stock.

7.	Add 30L of IAAC + Sel-Met + IPTG solution.  Grow overnight at 18C.  

Day 3: Harvest & Lysis
1.	Centrifuge your induction plate at 1700rcf for 15 minutes; discard supernatant and freeze pellets. 

2.	Prepare lysis buffer:
15 mL of 4X lysis buffer
45 mL of water
300 L of 1M DTT
1 tablet of Roche protease inhibitor
Mix thoroughly, then add:
20 L of rLysozyme and Benzonase

3.	Add 125 L of lysis buffer to each well of your frozen cell pellets.

4.	Vortex thoroughly, until all pellets are resuspended.

5.	Incubate at 25C, shaking, for 30 min.

6.	Freeze on dry ice, 15 min.

7.	Sonicate frozen plates for 1.5 min each, at around 250W.  Keep water bath as cold as possible.

8.	Freeze-sonicate plates (as in steps 4 and 5) twice more.

9.	Incubate at 25C, shaking, for 30 min.

10.	Freeze-sonicate plates (as in steps 4 and 5) three times.

11.	Remove 10uL of sonication mixture, and mix with 30 L of SDS loading buffer.  Boil and freeze.  This is your expression sample.

12.	Prepare TEV digestion mix:
0.5 mL 4X lysis buffer
1.5 mL water
10 L 1M DTT 
200 L 0.5M EDTA
3 mL TEV crude extract

13.	Add 10uL of TEV digestion mix to 90 L of sonication mixture in a new conical plate.

14.	Spin down at 1700rcf, (do not dump supernatant though) leave at 4C overnight.


Day 4.
1.	Spin down at 1700rcf.  Remove 40 L of the supernatant (make sure not to get any of the pellet).  Add to 20 L of 4X SDS loading buffer.  Boil and freeze.  This is your solubility sample.


Day 5.
Overview:  Purify plasmids from expressing clones, for storage and future transformation.

Hazards:  Normal precautions.  Procedure includes alkaline, acidic, combustible, and irritant solutions.

Materials: 	- Frozen pellets from starter cultures.
			- New deepwell plates.
			- Buffers: P1, P2, N3, PE, TE (or EB).
			- Turbo Filter and QiaPrep Filter.
			- New skirted plates.

Notes:  Use cone shape deepwell plates only.

1.	Resuspend frozen pellets in 150 L of Buffer P1.  Vortex thoroughly.

2.	Use Biomex FX to combine the best-expressing clones into one plate.

3.	Add 150 L of Buffer P2.  Shake gently, do not vortex.  Add N3 after 5 minutes.  This timing is important here try to get it right around 5 minutes.

4.	Add 250 L of Buffer N3.  Shake gently, do not vortex.

5.	Incubate on ice for ~20 minutes, to allow greater precipitation of ssDNA, KDS, etc.

6.	Proceed with FX program Plasmid Purification

MCSG-standard purification_ANL.name: standard purification_ANL
MCSG-standard purification_ANL.text:
Day 1  Small Culture (50mL)

Pick up cell culture from cloning lab. They will be in small, 2mL test tubes. Each tube contains a different target protein cloned in pMCSG7 (or other MCSG) vector and expressed in E.coli BL21 (DE3) cells. 

1.	Prepare M9 Pink Media by adding the following in a 1L bottle:

	1 pouch M9 Salts + NIAAC 
	10 mL Metal Supplement solution
	1 mL Kan/Amp/B1/B12 solution
	10 mL of 50% glycerol
	980 mL MQ water

2.	Aliquot 50 mL of M9 Pink Media in small, 250mL-plastic bottle
3.	Add 100 uL of LB cell culture 
4.	Shake in incubator overnight, 37 C, 150 rpm

Day 2  Large Culture (1 L) 

1.	Prepare M9 Pink Media as shown above, except add 930 mL of MQ water
2.	Add 25 mL of small culture from small plastic bottle to each 1 L bottle. Place an absorbent underpad on the cart prior to the transfer of bacterial cultures (e.g. Fisher # 14-206-63)). See special section at the end of this document for handling spills for this step.
3.	Shake in incubator at 37 C, 200 rpm until cells grow to OD 1.0 -1.4. You should start measuring OD (595 nm) after about 2.5-3 hours. 
4.	Add 30 mL of IAAC + Se-Met solution
5.	Transfer bottles to cooled 4 C incubator and shake for 1 hour
6.	Increase incubator temp to 18 C; induce the cells by adding 0.5 mL of 1 M IPTG 
7.	Grow cells at 18 C overnight

Day 3  Harvesting Cells

1.	Pour cell culture in 1L centrifuge bottle. Centrifuge for 8 minutes @ 7000 rpm, SS-6000 rotor (use the cart covered with an absorbent pad for liquid handling and see special section at the end of this document for handling spills)
2.	Dispose supernatant into 1:10 diluted bleach solution. Pour into sink after 20 minute incubation.
3.	Keep cells in 4 C  from now on
4.	add 1 tablet of Protease Inhibitor
5.	Re-suspend the cells by adding 25 mL of cold Lysis Buffer and gentle shaking
6.	Transfer resuspended cells into 50 mL Falcon tube and bring volume up to 40 mL with lysis buffer
7.	Freeze cells in -80 C freezer until they are ready to be purified

Day 4  IMAC 1*
*Note: AKTA must be stripped, charged, and blanked before actual purification run
1.	Thaw out cells - place in bucket of warm water for a few minutes. When thawed, transfer to ice (4 C )
2.	prepare Lysozyme stock solution: 50 mg/mL. Add Lysozyme to cells @ final concentration 1mg/mL
3.	Mix gently and keep cells on ice for 30 - 60 min
4.	Sonicate cells on ice for 3 minutes. Program: 4 seconds on 12 seconds off. Wear ear muffs during the procedure. After the sonication process is complete wait 5 minutes before opening the sonicator housing. Wipe the sonicator tip with gauze (wet the gauze with 10% bleach, allow 20 minutes of contact time), rinse the tip with distilled water and wipe. Discard the gauze in an autoclave bag.
5.	Transfer to 45 mL centrifuge tubes. Centrifuge for 1 hour @ 17,355 rpm, SS-34 rotor. Place an absorbent pad on the benchtop or cart during liquid transfer.
6.	Using 0.4 m syringe filter, filter supernatant into clean, 50 mL Falcon tube 
7.	Run Purification Program in AKTA Xpress

Buffers for AKTA Xpress

	Lysis Buffer	Elution Buffer	Desalting Buffer
HEPES pH 8.0	50 mM	50 mM	50 mM
NaCl	500 mM	500 mM	500 mM
Glycerol	5 %	5 %	5 %
*-mercaptoethanol	10 mM	10 mM	10 mM
*Imidazole	20 mM	250 mM	none
             *4X Buffer A does not contain these ingredients




To Prepare Buffers  add ingredients, stir, filter and store at 4 C

Stock Solution	Lysis Buffer
(4L)	Elution Buffer
(2L)	Desalting Buffer
(4L)
4X Buffer A	1 L	500 mL	1 L
14.3 M -mercaptoethanol	2.8 mL	1.4 mL	2.8 L
2.5 M Imidazole	32 mL	200 mL	None
MQ Water	Bring up to proper volume

Other Stock solutions needed for AKTA Xpress:
50 mM EDTA/0.5 M NaCl
100 mM NiSO4

Please use the laminated sheet and indicate the protein identifier(s) and your name for those targets of unknown function of RG2 microbes. The sheet must be attached to the chromatography refrigerator where the purifcation procedure takes place.

Day 5  TEV Cleavage
1.	Collect and combine fractions, keep everything at 4 C
2.	Take 50 uL of each pure protein sample. This will be the uncut samples  proteins that still contain His tags.
3.	Calculate amount of TEV protease needed
4.	Add TEV to remainder of protein sample
5.	Incubate proteins at 4 C refrigerator for 1-3 days
6.	Run SDS-PAGE to determine if tag cleavage has been successful. Use uncut protein samples as a reference point.
7.	If successful, run IMAC 2

Day ?  IMAC 2

1.	Add 4 mL of Ni-NTA slurry to a plastic disposable column
2.	Allow column to pack by letting liquid flow through
3.	Wash packed column with 20 mL MQ water
4.	Equilibrate with Lysis Buffer
5.	Slowly add protein sample using transfer pipette
6.	Collect flow-through sample right away
7.	Measure volume and concentration of protein
